fields.gwt:
- **Given** any graph written by the CLI
- **When** it is read and written again
- **Then** the bytes are identical: nodes sorted by type then ID, edges by (from, type, to), fixed key order, 2-space indent, no HTML escaping, trailing newline
- **And** `auto plan fmt <plan>` rewrites a hand-edited file into canonical form; `fmt --check` exits non-zero when it isn't
- **And** only malformed JSON fails to decode (`parse-error`); everything else is reported by validation with its JSON path
fields.title: graph.json is canonical and deterministic

fields.gwt:
- **Given** the schema
- **Then** goal, ac, decision, alternative, rail, defect, stage, file, question, tree, journey, leg and child exist, with required fields validated for presence and format
- **And** edge types are typed by their endpoints and a wrong endpoint type is rejected (`proves` is ac→goal only, `about` is tree→any, …)
fields.title: Every node type from the design is representable

fields.gwt:
- **Given** a plan at `lifecycle: requirements` holding only goals, questions and decisions
- **Then** lint reports no errors
- **And** at `solution`, `goal-no-ac` and `ac-no-verify` apply; at `plan`, stage and file coverage apply too
- **And** open `question` nodes report `open-question` as a gate at every step

fields.gwt:
- **Given** any mutating command
- **When** it succeeds
- **Then** stdout carries a top-level `id` plus the changed fields, and the file on disk is canonical
- **When** it would create an invalid graph
- **Then** it exits non-zero with `[]ValidationError` and a hint, and `graph.json` is **byte-identical** to before
fields.title: Writes are validated and atomic, and report what changed

fields.gwt:
- **Given** the real `auto` binary built from source and a fresh temp workspace
- **When** the `lifecycle` scenario runs init → new → add/link/update/unlink → a rejected write → retire → lifecycle → fmt → lint
- **Then** at every `# checkpoint` each `graph.json` is byte-identical to its snapshot
- **When** the `dogfood` scenario re-expresses epic 005, task 062 and task 052 from CLI commands alone
- **Then** every snapshot matches and `auto plan lint all` exits 0

fields.gwt:

fields.gwt:

- **And** it gets a `rank` after its last sibling; `move` changes only that node's rank

fields.gwt:

fields.why: Lint for a new type stays generic, and it adds a second file format to validate.

fields.chosen: The plan is always the first positional (or `all`); node IDs are plan-local; only cross-plan edge targets are qualified.
fields.title: Every command is auto plan <verb> <plan> [args]
fields.why: One mental model; plan resolution happens once, in shared argument parsing.

fields.chosen: Each plan holds one deterministic `graph.json` of typed nodes and edges; the CLI writes it and `auto plan lint` validates it.
fields.title: graph.json snapshot is the source of truth
fields.why: PR diffs read cleanly and hand edits stay possible; history comes from git, not the file.

fields.chosen: Node types, edge types and field specs live in `internal/schema/registry.go`; decode, lint, flags, cards, trace and docs all read it.
fields.title: The type registry is a Go table
fields.why: Fully typed validation and one format to maintain.

fields.chosen: A lowercase type prefix, a hyphen and 4 Crockford-base32 characters, regenerated on collision (retired included), never changed. The plan node's ID is `plan`.
fields.title: Node IDs are opaque: type prefix + 4 random base32 characters
fields.why: Removing or reordering never touches an ID, and branches don't collide.

fields.chosen: `plan.fields.lifecycle: requirements|solution|plan|executing|done` selects which rules apply, advanced by `update <plan> plan --lifecycle`.
fields.title: Lint is gated by an explicit lifecycle field
fields.why: A plan at `requirements` never errors for missing stages.

fields.chosen: The ordered steps are declared in `schema.Registry` next to the node and edge types; a test checks every referenced step exists.
fields.title: The lifecycle sequence lives in the registry
fields.why: A future version can change lifecycles without touching frozen plans.

fields.chosen: `add <plan> <type>` and `update <plan> <id>` expose one typed flag per field, generated at command build time; `@path` / `@-` reads long text.
fields.title: Typed per-type flags, generated from the registry
fields.why: Discoverable typed flags, and a new type gets flags with no CLI code.

fields.chosen: Exactly one node `plan` carries name, kind, lifecycle, epic and created date; plan-level relationships are edges from it; cross-plan references are `NNN:ID`.
fields.title: The plan header is a plan node; cross-plan refs are NNN:ID
fields.why: Every relationship lives in `edges[]`; plan numbers are unique across kinds ([[d-vg7q]]).

fields.chosen: Edges become `{id, from, type, to}` with `e-xxxx` IDs unique across the plan; `unlink` takes the ID or the triple.
fields.title: Edges get random IDs
fields.why: Review threads and evidence can anchor to edges; duplicate triples are still rejected.

fields.chosen: `auto plan` ships standalone; `new-task`, `new-solution`, `new-plan`, `new-epic` and `plan.html` keep working.
fields.title: Coexist with plan.html; planning skills untouched
fields.why: Adoption comes from follow-ups (skill migration, HTML renderer, importer) that build on this graph.

fields.chosen: No locking. `Save` writes a temp file and renames it into place.
fields.title: No write lock; atomic rename only
fields.why: Planners are serial, one agent per plan; git merges handle branches.

fields.chosen: Deliver everything in one task: a thin end-to-end path first (new → add/link G/AC/D → lint → show), then the remaining node types, lenses and epics.
fields.title: One task, staged as a walking skeleton
fields.why: The real binary judges every stage from the first commit; epics can split off if the task proves too big.

fields.chosen: `auto plan renumber <plan> [--to NNN]` renames the folder, rewrites the plan ID (keeping its suffix) and every reference in writable plans; refuses with `frozen-ref`.
fields.title: Number collisions are fixed at merge time by renumber
fields.why: The ID always matches its folder; rewriting is fine because plans stay mutable until they merge.

fields.chosen: `new` generates `NNN-xxxx`, stored as graph.json's top-level `id`; qualified references store the full ID; the CLI expands the `NNN` shorthand when unambiguous.
fields.title: Each plan has its own ID: NNN-xxxx
fields.why: References stay unambiguous while two branches have both allocated the same number. Decided after execution, during PR #157.

fields.chosen: `version` is a semver string starting at `1.0.0`; writes are refused (`frozen`) on a major mismatch or once lifecycle is `done`.
fields.title: Semver schema versions; plans freeze instead of migrating
fields.why: A new schema version only affects plans created after it; completed plans are a permanent record.

fields.chosen: `auto plan new` creates `docs/plans/NNN-name/`; tasks and epics share one root and one numbering sequence, and the graph records `kind`.
fields.title: Plans live in docs/plans/NNN-name/, for both kinds
fields.why: Existing task and epic docs stay untouched, and one sequence keeps `NNN` unambiguous across kinds.

fields.chosen: The canonical plans root is `.auto/plan/plans/NNN-name/graph.json`; everything else in [[d-vg7q]] still holds.
fields.title: Plans live in .auto/plan/plans/, not docs/plans/ (amends D-1)
fields.why: Plans are tool-owned data and follow the `.auto/<tool>/` convention; `docs/` stays prose for people.

fields.chosen: The hierarchy stays epic → task.
fields.title: Keep two levels (epic → task) for now
fields.why: No use case for deeper nesting has come up; versioning lets a later version add it.

fields.chosen: Generic node envelopes `{id,type,status,fields}` and a separate typed edges array `{from,type,to}`, both validated by the registry.
fields.title: graph.json is generic nodes[] + edges[]
fields.why: A literal, uniformly queryable graph; new edge types never touch node shapes.

fields.chosen: Each node has a sortable `rank`; `move --before|--after` writes one new rank. Stages render in `dependsOn` order, ACs under their goal via `proves`.
fields.title: Reading order is a rank field; meaningful order stays in edges
fields.why: Inserts and reorders are single-field changes that merge cleanly.

fields.body:
lint(plan)
  Decode(path)  tolerant: only malformed JSON fails
  Validate(graph)  every structural issue as data
  rules(lifecycle)  gated by plan.lifecycle
write(plan, op)
  Decode(path)
  mutate(op)
  Validate(graph)  refuse on any error, file untouched
  Save(path)  canonical sort, temp file + rename
fields.title: Two gates: tolerant lint, strict writes

fields.body:
auto-plan/
├── cmd/autoplan/main.go  entry point
├── rootcmd/rootcmd.go  mounting façade for auto-cli
└── internal/
    ├── schema/  the type registry, the only extension point
    ├── graph/  decode, validate, mutate, canonical save
    ├── workspace/  plans root, numbering, plan-argument resolution
    ├── lint/  lifecycle-gated rules, epic rules, Tarjan cycles
    ├── tree/  show-me parser and renderer
    ├── render/  show, card, trace and brief views
    └── cli/  cobra verbs with registry-generated flags
fields.title: The auto-plan module

fields.body:
auto plan add <plan> <type>
  schema.Registry.Node(type)  flags generated per FieldSpec
  graph.Decode
  graph.Add  new ID, rank after the last sibling
    graph.Validate
  graph.Save
